ca_snag_crag.blurb: Snag Crag is a small bolted wall in Land of the Lost, a cluster of quartzite crags on Horse Mountain that is the nearest sport climbing to Arcata and Eureka. All eight routes are sport climbs: short, steep and well featured. Grades start around 5.9 and climb to 5.12, with five of them at 5.10 and one each at 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits climbers working through the 5.10s. The base is a five-minute hike from the lot shared with Pinch Me Wall, marked by a big boulder at the foot of a small gully.

ca_tea_room_the.blurb: The Tea Room is an alcove on the terrace beside the Black Face at the far east end of Echo Cliffs, in the Santa Monica Mountains near Los Angeles. It has eight routes, seven of them sport and one top rope, and the grades stay tight: a single 5.9 and the rest in the 5.10 range. The wall stays mostly shaded. The terrace is reached by a short, easy fourth-class scramble up from the base trail. The routes are among the newest at Echo Cliffs and have seen limited traffic, so loose holds are possible and a helmet makes sense.

ca_toller_tower.blurb: Toller Tower is a small cliff band rather than a true tower, on Burst Rock beside Sonora Pass Highway at roughly 8,570 feet. All eight routes are trad. Grades run from one very easy line up to two 5.10 climbs, with most in the 5.6 to 5.8 band. The base is reached by walking down Broadway Gully from the Burst Rock Trail; the cliff sits on the right side of the gully, about halfway down. Most routes begin from a wide ledge that takes a few feet of fourth-class climbing to reach.

ca_south_pole.blurb: South Pole is a trad cliff on the Negropolis Hillside in the Quail Springs area of Joshua Tree National Park, about two-thirds of the way up the slope between the North Pole and Snooze Rock formations. It has eight routes, seven trad and one top rope, graded from 5.5 up to 5.9, with most between 5.7 and 5.9. The cliffs are generally in shade. From the roadside parking at the west end of the Negropolis, walk around the end of the rockpile on flat ground, continue along the base of the hill for roughly 400 yards, then climb the slope to the wall.

ca_planet_x_pinnacle.blurb: Planet X Pinnacle is a free-standing pinnacle on the south side of the Planet X boulder field, east of The Love Nest in Joshua Tree National Park. Routes go up every side. It has eight problems and routes: four trad leads, two top ropes and two boulder problems. The roped climbs run from 5.8 to 5.10, including a hand crack and a thin, crimpy line. The nearby boulders pull most of the visitors, so the pinnacle itself is usually left to a few parties. Planet X Area, its parent, also holds the Love Nest and the Crypt.

ca_struggler_cliff.blurb: Struggler Cliff is a short, dome-like cliff of about 20 feet in the Cosumnes River Gorge near Placerville, on the west side of the North Fork. It has eight routes, mostly easy top ropes up knobby faces plus a pair of wide cracks, and the anchors are bolts on top. Five of the routes are 5.8 or easier, with a couple at 5.9 and 5.10, and three can also be led on trad gear. From the road, follow the main trail down Dinkum Gully to the foot of Bucks Bar Dome, take the right fork, and the cliff sits about 30 feet along.

ca_the_elements.blurb: The Elements is a steep sport crag near the town of Mount Shasta, across the road from Ney Springs at about 3,300 feet. It has eight routes, seven sport and one trad, and the difficulty is concentrated high: one easy 5.5, a 5.10 and a 5.11, then four 5.12s and a 5.13. Expect small holds and slight overhangs where crimp strength and a stick clip help. In low water the walk from the Ney Springs parking is about five to ten minutes, ending by climbing the slope past a mossy lower cliff to the crag above it.
